item.title: Trump says U.S. bombed Kharg Island, striking core of Iran’s oil economy
item.summary: About 90 percent of the country’s oil exports move through facilities on Kharg Island, located some 15 miles from the mainland in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Hegseth vows thorough probe of school strike that Trump blamed on Iran
item.summary: The announcement appeared to tacitly acknowledge a growing body of evidence that U.S. forces, not Iran, were responsible for the deadly attack.

item.title: 6 dead after U.S. Air Force refueler crashes in Iraq while supporting Iran war
item.summary: The KC-135 tanker was involved in an apparent accident with another KC-135. The other aircraft landed safely, officials said.

item.title: Former NFL players decry White House video mixing big hits, airstrikes
item.summary: The Trump administration released a video on X using footage of Ray Lewis, Chad Ochocinco and other former NFL players juxtaposed with war footage.

item.title: U.S. sailors injured in fire aboard aircraft carrier supporting Iran war
item.summary: The incident, in a laundry room on the USS Gerald R. Ford, is another setback during the ship’s extended deployment.

item.title: We asked 1,000 Americans if U.S. strikes on Iran should continue. Here’s what they said.
item.summary: Resistance to the U.S. military campaign in Iran is easing overall, though a plurality of Americans still favor ending the strikes.

item.title: Trump is counting on his ‘favorite Mormon’ to deliver health care wins
item.summary: Chris Klomp, a political unknown a year ago, is now steering the $2.6 trillion health department. Several controversial appointees have since left.

item.title: Can Florida save Trump’s plan to keep GOP in power?
item.summary: Republicans in Florida say they may not be able to deliver the type of redistricting bonanza that would give the party breathing room in the midterms.

item.title: White House proposes new visitor screening center to access grounds
item.summary: The 33,000-square-foot screening center, planned below Sherman Park, would be the Trump administration’s latest effort to remake the White House grounds.

item.title: Sinema acknowledges affair with Senate bodyguard while in office
item.summary: The acknowledgement is part of a legal filing to dismiss an “alienation of affection” lawsuit against the former senator from Arizona.
